claims.quote: A property checks that an aggregate over candidates it may not combine, such as numbers that are not whole beside text, gives the same and fails naming the same value whatever order the facts came in. The mutation that combined such candidates in the order they came, named for sums of numbers that are not whole, could not fail any property, since every aggregate's fold is the same in any order; what the order decides is which value the error names. It is now named for that, and the property catches it within 3 runs.

The weights properties now follow changes of several facts at once, which can make several invented mothers given in one change beside a registered mother. Two rows with one key that met while their unknowns were free can then part after both became given, and only the note of what they gave when they met takes it away: the mutation that asked the unknowns facts hold now instead, missed in 60,000 runs of one-fact changes, fails within 200.
